B0CZKYMVPR#28.review: Check your wiring first, but very convenient when it works - The thing you need to know before buying this switch remote and receiver is that the receiver requires four wires, which not every light switch box will have. It depends on how your lightswitch was installed. So, I recommend turning off the breaker and opening up the switch you want to move to check the wiring before ordering. Make sure there’s a cable with power coming in (live black wire and neutral white). This will power the receiver. If there are only two wires, then power is going to the fixture first, and the receiver won’t work. There also needs to be a cable with two wires going to the fixture. If there’s a third, red wire, you probably have a 3-way switch. Treewell does sell a receiver with two remotes for this situation (see my review of that below). I installed mine to move a switch for the light over our kitchen sink. The original switch was awkwardly placed behind where we keep our dish soap, etc. I put the new switch on the side of the cabinet above and to the right of the sink. It was great not to have to run wires or take up cabinet space with an electrical box. If you are moving a switch, you might want to go ahead and order a blank wall plate to match your box size and decor. At first, I thought it might feel wasteful to use a battery powered switch, but most ceiling fans have remotes now, so it’s not that unusual. I plan to install a garbage disposal, and I’m thinking about getting another one of these switches for that. Great product! ------------------------------------------------------------ Here's my review of the 3-way version (also 5 stars): Our new house has a Jack and Jill bathroom. The inspector said one of the light switches was too close to the bathtub. I was able to install this receiver where the old switch was and install the new remote switch on the other side of the doorway. The bathroom has pocket doors, so I wouldn’t have been able to move the switch to the new location without this product. I needed the version with 2 remotes because this is a 3-way switch. I couldn’t figure out the wiring to replace only 1 of the switches. So, I replaced them both. I capped off the extra wires going between the two switches (even though there’s no power going to those wires now). There was just enough room in the single-gang box to fit everything back inside. It’s nice that they include both bolts and screws/anchors to install the remote switch plates, allowing you to mount the plates to electrical boxes or the wall. I’m realizing now that I could also move the second switch inside the bathroom. I might do that later. This system is very flexible with lots of applications.

B08RRM8VH5#40.review: A reasonable replacement for the seemingly deprecated DG6HD - TLDR: This is working well with Matter and Home Assistant over wifi; if I have any issues with reliability I will update. Note: I have many Zigbee "gen 1" Leviton dimmers DG6HD. They are still (mostly) my favorite excepting two things, 1 they seem to be at least softly discontinued, not advertised anymore and hard to find in stock, 2: the D26HD supports double tap to max brightness, which the Zigbee DG6HD does not have. Because of these 2 reasons, I reluctantly tried the D26HD and find it an acceptable alternative; however, I'd still prefer a Thread or Zigbee-based version as D26HD requires a My Leviton account, access to your wifi, access to your precision location on your mobile, access to your wi-fi password, and Internet access, and is harder to set up than Zigbee switches for those who know what is Zigbee and have a Zigbee hub. If you want Matter you have to use My Leviton to set it up first, opt into Matter early access, and upgrade your firmware. This was "easy enough". Not as easy as Zigbee you click one button in Home Assistant and done though. The Zigbee versions also allow access to fade in/out timers, but Matter mode does not, at least in HA as of writing this review; however, you can configure it via My Leviton app. I have not yet tested if the device works when restricted from the Internet in Matter mode. I use this with the DD00R companion for multi-location dimming. I did not want to use the "anywhere" battery-operated switches so utilized existing multi-pole wiring. Wiring is standard. Compared to DG6HD's screw terminals the D26HD uses pigtails -- some find this as a pro, some as con. The DD00R is compatible with the double tap to max on / off, which surprised me since it was made for gen 1 devices that don't support it; HOWEVER, if you double tap the DD00R quickly it recognizes as a single tap while on the D26HD it works perfectly. Using remote control via My Leviton and via Matter through Home Assistant appears instant. I opted to use My Leviton as little as possible so I use Google Assistant integration via Home Assistant instead of My Leviton. In Home Assistant Matter only the on/off and dim level is supported, which for me supports all everyday use case. In My Leviton you can change bulb type, min and max dim power levels, and fade on and fade off time settings in 0.5 second increments and upgrade firmware, which is a "one time" expected use for me. In general, I am anti-wifi for smart devices due to the lower reliability I've typically witnessed and inappropriate for battery-powered devices, but as a wired device it is OK enough, although if Leviton drops cloud support you lose the advanced configuration functionality. I still prefer the privacy-centric features and cloud-free Zigbee DG6HD, but again they seem to be on the way out. A great improvement will be when Matter comes out-of-the-box so you can enroll it without Internet or My Leviton, and if the advanced features can be supported (if possible) via Matter.

B08RRM8VH5#40.review: A reasonable replacement for the seemingly deprecated DG6HD - TLDR: This is working well with Matter and Home Assistant over wifi; if I have any issues with reliability I will update. Note: I have many Zigbee "gen 1" Leviton dimmers DG6HD. They are still (mostly) my favorite excepting two things, 1 they seem to be at least softly discontinued, not advertised anymore and hard to find in stock, 2: the D26HD supports double tap to max brightness, which the Zigbee DG6HD does not have. Because of these 2 reasons, I reluctantly tried the D26HD and find it an acceptable alternative; however, I'd still prefer a Thread or Zigbee-based version as D26HD requires a My Leviton account, access to your wifi, access to your precision location on your mobile, access to your wi-fi password, and Internet access, and is harder to set up than Zigbee switches for those who know what is Zigbee and have a Zigbee hub. If you want Matter you have to use My Leviton to set it up first, opt into Matter early access, and upgrade your firmware. This was "easy enough". Not as easy as Zigbee you click one button in Home Assistant and done though. The Zigbee versions also allow access to fade in/out timers, but Matter mode does not, at least in HA as of writing this review; however, you can configure it via My Leviton app. I have not yet tested if the device works when restricted from the Internet in Matter mode. I use this with the DD00R companion for multi-location dimming. I did not want to use the "anywhere" battery-operated switches so utilized existing multi-pole wiring. Wiring is standard. Compared to DG6HD's screw terminals the D26HD uses pigtails -- some find this as a pro, some as con. The DD00R is compatible with the double tap to max on / off, which surprised me since it was made for gen 1 devices that don't support it; HOWEVER, if you double tap the DD00R quickly it recognizes as a single tap while on the D26HD it works perfectly. Using remote control via My Leviton and via Matter through Home Assistant appears instant. I opted to use My Leviton as little as possible so I use Google Assistant integration via Home Assistant instead of My Leviton. In Home Assistant Matter only the on/off and dim level is supported, which for me supports all everyday use case. In My Leviton you can change bulb type, min and max dim power levels, and fade on and fade off time settings in 0.5 second increments and upgrade firmware, which is a "one time" expected use for me. In general, I am anti-wifi for smart devices due to the lower reliability I've typically witnessed and inappropriate for battery-powered devices, but as a wired device it is OK enough, although if Leviton drops cloud support you lose the advanced configuration functionality. I still prefer the privacy-centric features and cloud-free Zigbee DG6HD, but again they seem to be on the way out. A great improvement will be when Matter comes out-of-the-box so you can enroll it without Internet or My Leviton, and if the advanced features can be supported (if possible) via Matter.

A few things to note: 1) If installing using a standard switch as the other switch, you may not choose which light switch it replaces, the smart switch MUST replace the load switch (connected to the light fixture), and you MUST make a minor modification to the way the standard switch is wired. I didn't realize this when I ordered, and was not able to position the smart switch at the most convenient of the two switch locations. 2) The instructions include a wiring diagram, but unless you are comfortable and familiar with identifying which wires in your walls are what, you may have difficulty. It is not as simple as red-to-red, black-to-black. In my case, red had to go to a black wire, brown went to red, and so on. 3) Overall, the switch functions as I'd expect, with the exception that when set below 75% and the light starts in OFF with the switch DOWN, the standard switch must be toggled on and off twice for the light to turn off. Above 75% brightness, the standard switch functions as normal, and if the light is ON with the switch DOWN, the switch functions as normal. Its odd, but not a deal breaker. I even tried a replacement smart switch, but experienced the same behavior. See my video demonstrating the quirky behavior. You can find a very helpful video on youtube if you search for the video titled "Correctly Install Amazon WiFi 3 Way Smart Switch" by The Home Improvement Channel

B095X5HTLS#37.review: YMMV: Did not work with only my LED fixture and a traditional 3 way switch in the circuit - I was a little leery that the online description as of 04/06/24 said this switch uses just one traveler wire. 3 way circuits always have two travelers. But I wanted to check it out their innovation as I have Amazon plugs and Echos in my house. I have also installed multiple single pole and 3 way smart switches from other brands. I know how to wire two travelers, I've got neutral wires, and my existing setup had two working standard 3 way switches that functioned just fine. BTW, the included instructions showed a different wiring setup than the one in the product description. Unfortunately, neither worked for my setup. 5 stars for innovation reduced to 1 star for execution. The positive: once it was hooked up, Alexa did automatically sense the switch, connect to WiFi, and add it to My Devices. The negatives: I was never able to get the switch to function as designed with my LED fixture, the Amazon switch, and a standard switch in the circuit. I am assuming this may have something to do with the low power draw or the dimmer function (not likely, I know). In the best wiring configuration - I tried them all - I could turn the fixture on and off from the Alexa app - but once I used the standard switch it turned off and would only flicker on briefly when I flipped the standard switch. Also, when the fixture was lit it buzzed (search for the other brands that use the technology that eliminates this). No shorts, not incorrect wiring. I disconnected all the wiring, started from scratch, and used an NCV and a meter to confirm the continuity on each wire. Same results. I swapped the smart switch with the standard switch just in case I incorrectly identified the "load" side. Same results. I put the old standard 3 way switch back and everything worked with no buzz. Insanity is trying the same thing over and over with the same results. So I am returning this switch and suggest that if you are using a single low power LED fixture and a standard switch you try a smart switch that accommodates two travelers in its wiring, doesn't need to be on the "load" side, and doesn't cause buzzing.

B095X5HTLS#37.review: YMMV: Did not work with only my LED fixture and a traditional 3 way switch in the circuit - I was a little leery that the online description as of 04/06/24 said this switch uses just one traveler wire. 3 way circuits always have two travelers. But I wanted to check it out their innovation as I have Amazon plugs and Echos in my house. I have also installed multiple single pole and 3 way smart switches from other brands. I know how to wire two travelers, I've got neutral wires, and my existing setup had two working standard 3 way switches that functioned just fine. BTW, the included instructions showed a different wiring setup than the one in the product description. Unfortunately, neither worked for my setup. 5 stars for innovation reduced to 1 star for execution. The positive: once it was hooked up, Alexa did automatically sense the switch, connect to WiFi, and add it to My Devices. The negatives: I was never able to get the switch to function as designed with my LED fixture, the Amazon switch, and a standard switch in the circuit. I am assuming this may have something to do with the low power draw or the dimmer function (not likely, I know). In the best wiring configuration - I tried them all - I could turn the fixture on and off from the Alexa app - but once I used the standard switch it turned off and would only flicker on briefly when I flipped the standard switch. Also, when the fixture was lit it buzzed (search for the other brands that use the technology that eliminates this). No shorts, not incorrect wiring. I disconnected all the wiring, started from scratch, and used an NCV and a meter to confirm the continuity on each wire. Same results. I swapped the smart switch with the standard switch just in case I incorrectly identified the "load" side. Same results. I put the old standard 3 way switch back and everything worked with no buzz. Insanity is trying the same thing over and over with the same results. So I am returning this switch and suggest that if you are using a single low power LED fixture and a standard switch you try a smart switch that accommodates two travelers in its wiring, doesn't need to be on the "load" side, and doesn't cause buzzing.

This switch comes with a nice screwless wall plate, which you can use if you have a lone switch to replace. It easily connects with your wifi system using your phone and the MyLeviton app, where you can set up schedules for on and off times, including basing them on sundown or sunrise. For instance, I set mine to come on ten minutes after sunset and go off at 10:30pm, every day. Now, installation: Is this for a DIYer or for an electrician to install? If you know nothing about house wiring, don't plan on doing this yourself. Nothing wrong with how it's built, but you can run into interesting issues when you open a box with, say, three or four other switches in it. It may seem to have a confusing jumble of wires, the switch you're replacing may have no neutral (white) coming to it, and you'll need to figure out which wire goes to the source and which goes to the load. All that said, if you DO know what you're doing with house wiring, this is a snap to install (aside from the problems just mentioned). The switch is likely larger than the one you're replacing, and there may be scant room for it. The switch has wires coming out of it (i.e., no screw terminals or insert holes) that you attach to existing wiring with wire nuts, and you need to cram all that in the box. Note that this switch can be used in two-way or three-way configurations. Full disclosure, I have used it only in two-way on/off applications.

B08RRM8VH5#40.review: A reasonable replacement for the seemingly deprecated DG6HD - TLDR: This is working well with Matter and Home Assistant over wifi; if I have any issues with reliability I will update. Note: I have many Zigbee "gen 1" Leviton dimmers DG6HD. They are still (mostly) my favorite excepting two things, 1 they seem to be at least softly discontinued, not advertised anymore and hard to find in stock, 2: the D26HD supports double tap to max brightness, which the Zigbee DG6HD does not have. Because of these 2 reasons, I reluctantly tried the D26HD and find it an acceptable alternative; however, I'd still prefer a Thread or Zigbee-based version as D26HD requires a My Leviton account, access to your wifi, access to your precision location on your mobile, access to your wi-fi password, and Internet access, and is harder to set up than Zigbee switches for those who know what is Zigbee and have a Zigbee hub. If you want Matter you have to use My Leviton to set it up first, opt into Matter early access, and upgrade your firmware. This was "easy enough". Not as easy as Zigbee you click one button in Home Assistant and done though. The Zigbee versions also allow access to fade in/out timers, but Matter mode does not, at least in HA as of writing this review; however, you can configure it via My Leviton app. I have not yet tested if the device works when restricted from the Internet in Matter mode. I use this with the DD00R companion for multi-location dimming. I did not want to use the "anywhere" battery-operated switches so utilized existing multi-pole wiring. Wiring is standard. Compared to DG6HD's screw terminals the D26HD uses pigtails -- some find this as a pro, some as con. The DD00R is compatible with the double tap to max on / off, which surprised me since it was made for gen 1 devices that don't support it; HOWEVER, if you double tap the DD00R quickly it recognizes as a single tap while on the D26HD it works perfectly. Using remote control via My Leviton and via Matter through Home Assistant appears instant. I opted to use My Leviton as little as possible so I use Google Assistant integration via Home Assistant instead of My Leviton. In Home Assistant Matter only the on/off and dim level is supported, which for me supports all everyday use case. In My Leviton you can change bulb type, min and max dim power levels, and fade on and fade off time settings in 0.5 second increments and upgrade firmware, which is a "one time" expected use for me. In general, I am anti-wifi for smart devices due to the lower reliability I've typically witnessed and inappropriate for battery-powered devices, but as a wired device it is OK enough, although if Leviton drops cloud support you lose the advanced configuration functionality. I still prefer the privacy-centric features and cloud-free Zigbee DG6HD, but again they seem to be on the way out. A great improvement will be when Matter comes out-of-the-box so you can enroll it without Internet or My Leviton, and if the advanced features can be supported (if possible) via Matter.
aspects: 31207#dimming: works perfectly with double tap feature

B08RRM8VH5#40.review: A reasonable replacement for the seemingly deprecated DG6HD - TLDR: This is working well with Matter and Home Assistant over wifi; if I have any issues with reliability I will update. Note: I have many Zigbee "gen 1" Leviton dimmers DG6HD. They are still (mostly) my favorite excepting two things, 1 they seem to be at least softly discontinued, not advertised anymore and hard to find in stock, 2: the D26HD supports double tap to max brightness, which the Zigbee DG6HD does not have. Because of these 2 reasons, I reluctantly tried the D26HD and find it an acceptable alternative; however, I'd still prefer a Thread or Zigbee-based version as D26HD requires a My Leviton account, access to your wifi, access to your precision location on your mobile, access to your wi-fi password, and Internet access, and is harder to set up than Zigbee switches for those who know what is Zigbee and have a Zigbee hub. If you want Matter you have to use My Leviton to set it up first, opt into Matter early access, and upgrade your firmware. This was "easy enough". Not as easy as Zigbee you click one button in Home Assistant and done though. The Zigbee versions also allow access to fade in/out timers, but Matter mode does not, at least in HA as of writing this review; however, you can configure it via My Leviton app. I have not yet tested if the device works when restricted from the Internet in Matter mode. I use this with the DD00R companion for multi-location dimming. I did not want to use the "anywhere" battery-operated switches so utilized existing multi-pole wiring. Wiring is standard. Compared to DG6HD's screw terminals the D26HD uses pigtails -- some find this as a pro, some as con. The DD00R is compatible with the double tap to max on / off, which surprised me since it was made for gen 1 devices that don't support it; HOWEVER, if you double tap the DD00R quickly it recognizes as a single tap while on the D26HD it works perfectly. Using remote control via My Leviton and via Matter through Home Assistant appears instant. I opted to use My Leviton as little as possible so I use Google Assistant integration via Home Assistant instead of My Leviton. In Home Assistant Matter only the on/off and dim level is supported, which for me supports all everyday use case. In My Leviton you can change bulb type, min and max dim power levels, and fade on and fade off time settings in 0.5 second increments and upgrade firmware, which is a "one time" expected use for me. In general, I am anti-wifi for smart devices due to the lower reliability I've typically witnessed and inappropriate for battery-powered devices, but as a wired device it is OK enough, although if Leviton drops cloud support you lose the advanced configuration functionality. I still prefer the privacy-centric features and cloud-free Zigbee DG6HD, but again they seem to be on the way out. A great improvement will be when Matter comes out-of-the-box so you can enroll it without Internet or My Leviton, and if the advanced features can be supported (if possible) via Matter.

B095X5HTLS#37.review: YMMV: Did not work with only my LED fixture and a traditional 3 way switch in the circuit - I was a little leery that the online description as of 04/06/24 said this switch uses just one traveler wire. 3 way circuits always have two travelers. But I wanted to check it out their innovation as I have Amazon plugs and Echos in my house. I have also installed multiple single pole and 3 way smart switches from other brands. I know how to wire two travelers, I've got neutral wires, and my existing setup had two working standard 3 way switches that functioned just fine. BTW, the included instructions showed a different wiring setup than the one in the product description. Unfortunately, neither worked for my setup. 5 stars for innovation reduced to 1 star for execution. The positive: once it was hooked up, Alexa did automatically sense the switch, connect to WiFi, and add it to My Devices. The negatives: I was never able to get the switch to function as designed with my LED fixture, the Amazon switch, and a standard switch in the circuit. I am assuming this may have something to do with the low power draw or the dimmer function (not likely, I know). In the best wiring configuration - I tried them all - I could turn the fixture on and off from the Alexa app - but once I used the standard switch it turned off and would only flicker on briefly when I flipped the standard switch. Also, when the fixture was lit it buzzed (search for the other brands that use the technology that eliminates this). No shorts, not incorrect wiring. I disconnected all the wiring, started from scratch, and used an NCV and a meter to confirm the continuity on each wire. Same results. I swapped the smart switch with the standard switch just in case I incorrectly identified the "load" side. Same results. I put the old standard 3 way switch back and everything worked with no buzz. Insanity is trying the same thing over and over with the same results. So I am returning this switch and suggest that if you are using a single low power LED fixture and a standard switch you try a smart switch that accommodates two travelers in its wiring, doesn't need to be on the "load" side, and doesn't cause buzzing.

B0BVKZLT3B#23.review: Easy to set up with an on/off schedule... - First, Leviton is high quality, no question. This is not my first automatic Leviton switch, this was a second buy. It easily connects with your wifi system using your phone and the MyLeviton app, where you can set up schedules for on and off times, including basing them on sundown or sunrise. For instance, I set mine to come on ten minutes after sunset and go off at 10:30pm, every day. Now, installation: Is this for a DIYer or for an electrician to install? If you know nothing about house wiring, don't plan on doing this yourself. Nothing wrong with how it's built, but you can run into interesting issues when you open a box with, say, three or four other switches in it. It may seem to have a confusing jumble of wires, the switch you're replacing may have no neutral (white) coming to it, and you'll need to figure out which wire goes to the source and which goes to the load. All that said, if you DO know what you're doing with house wiring, this is a snap to install (aside from the problems just mentioned). The switch is likely larger than the one you're replacing, and there may be scant room for it. The switch has wires coming out of it (i.e., no screw terminals or insert holes) that you attach to existing wiring with wire nuts, and you need to cram all that in the box. Note that this switch can be used in two-way or three-way configurations. Full disclosure, I have used it only in two-way on/off applications.

Setup was straightforward, but my experience took a drastic turn when I attempted to add the switch to HomeKit using Matter. Firstly, this switch does not support Matter out of the box. You are required to enroll in a beta program and install beta firmware on the switch to enable Matter functionality. Even after doing so, I encountered persistent issues. Despite numerous attempts to connect, including resetting the device, restarting my router and phone, and trying every troubleshooting step I could find, the switch simply would not pair with HomeKit via Matter. After some research, I discovered forum posts suggesting that Matter requires a 2.4GHz-only Wi-Fi network. I have a Google Nest Wi-Fi Pro router, which doesn’t allow disabling specific Wi-Fi bands. It's worth noting that I have several other Matter-enabled devices from different brands that connected seamlessly without needing to adjust any network settings. I even exchanged the switch for a new one, thinking I might have received a faulty unit, but the problem persisted. Leviton's claim that this switch supports Matter is, in my opinion, misleading. You’re required to A) sign up for a beta program, B) install beta firmware, and C) have a router that allows disabling specific Wi-Fi bands—all of which other brands do not require for their Matter-enabled devices. In summary, if you’re looking for a seamless Matter experience, this switch is not the way to go.

B00004YUO0#2.review: How is this product rated so highly? - This is my experience. How else can I rate a product except by personal experience? For many years, replacing a light switch was a no-brainer. Not in terms of being careless; one does not fool around with electricity (or plumbing). I mean in terms of going to the store and buying a Leviton light switch. Good quality and highly dependable. Well, I am sorry but I think something bad has happened in recent years at Leviton. In a nutshell, my experience is this: I have Leviton light switches that probably go back to when my house was new (circa 1980) and they go on and on, no problem. Never need replacing. However, with a handful of switches that did need replacing in recent years, I have needed to replace them more than once. Especially, in one case, a bathroom light switch. FOUR TIMES IN THE PAST TWO OR THREE YEARS. This is not a high-traffic area and there are no children playing with or abusing this switch. My wife and I are consciously taking it easy with this one, knowing that it keeps breaking. There is nothing in the way that it is installed that would account for it being fragile. Yet, here I was the other night, with my wife informing me that the bathroom light switch was broken again. This necessitated a trip to Home Depot which fortunately stays open until 10pm. And get this: A Home Depot employee approached me while I was looking for alternatives, offering me assistance. I asked him what in the heck is wrong with this type of Leviton light switch. "It keeps breaking?" he said. "Yes," I said. He did not say anything else in response but he did nod his head in agreement, like it's not the first time he has heard this. My theory is, some time in the past few years, Leviton decided to go with a lower-grade of plastic in order to save money. What else would account for this repeated failure? And it's not just a bad batch; I have gone to both Ace Hardware and Home Depot over a long enough period of time with the same bad results for replacing Leviton light switches in the bathroom and two other locations in my house. Unasked, the Home Depot guy recommended that I go with a rocker type of switch instead. "Better quality," was his advice. I hope so because it, too, is made by Leviton. For one thing is true: Leviton sure as heck has the local retail market sewn up. We may see alternatives here on Amazon but in places like Home Depot, Leviton is all that is available.

I mean in terms of going to the store and buying a Leviton light switch. Good quality and highly dependable. Well, I am sorry but I think something bad has happened in recent years at Leviton. In a nutshell, my experience is this: I have Leviton light switches that probably go back to when my house was new (circa 1980) and they go on and on, no problem. Never need replacing. However, with a handful of switches that did need replacing in recent years, I have needed to replace them more than once. Especially, in one case, a bathroom light switch. FOUR TIMES IN THE PAST TWO OR THREE YEARS. This is not a high-traffic area and there are no children playing with or abusing this switch. My wife and I are consciously taking it easy with this one, knowing that it keeps breaking. There is nothing in the way that it is installed that would account for it being fragile. Yet, here I was the other night, with my wife informing me that the bathroom light switch was broken again. This necessitated a trip to Home Depot which fortunately stays open until 10pm. And get this: A Home Depot employee approached me while I was looking for alternatives, offering me assistance. I asked him what in the heck is wrong with this type of Leviton light switch. "It keeps breaking?" he said. "Yes," I said. He did not say anything else in response but he did nod his head in agreement, like it's not the first time he has heard this. My theory is, some time in the past few years, Leviton decided to go with a lower-grade of plastic in order to save money. What else would account for this repeated failure? And it's not just a bad batch; I have gone to both Ace Hardware and Home Depot over a long enough period of time with the same bad results for replacing Leviton light switches in the bathroom and two other locations in my house. Unasked, the Home Depot guy recommended that I go with a rocker type of switch instead. "Better quality," was his advice. I hope so because it, too, is made by Leviton. For one thing is true: Leviton sure as heck has the local retail market sewn up. We may see alternatives here on Amazon but in places like Home Depot, Leviton is all that is available.

Hopefully this will help someone else. - When I installed the switch, I have neutral wires in my gangboxes (house built in 2000), and was shocked that this switch didn't have a neutral connection. You don't need it for this switch, which is great for those that don't have the wire, but it was a first for me as my Zwave switches always needed it - Switch was installed correctly, but had no lights on the switch itself, and while I noticed my outdoor porch lights were showing a dimly lit bulb, hitting the on or off on the switch did nothing. I was convinced initially it was wiring, but lo and behold, the true issue was the bulbs that I installed. I had purchased some cheap no-name brand LED bulbs and they were not dimmable (I think). Upon changing the bulb, the switch showed operational lights, and everything worked fine. In my two fixtures, I initially only changed one, and that was all it took to get it working. I confirmed the same issue when I installed another switch for my 3 deck post lights. Changing a bulb to a dimmable bulb (while I wait for matching replacements) was all I needed to do to get it to work! - Pico remotes are amazing, and can be used for many different things. Love that I don't need hardwired Z-wave accessory switches anymore, and these make it so less crowded in a multi-gangbox! Highly recommend those looking to make the switch from Zwave, WiFi and other lower quality switches. I will say my Zwave installation was flawless in operation, but ultimately got sick of the low quality and frequent failures. Anyone considering a "WiFi" switch should not do so, but I'm not going to gain much in functionality over my Zwave switches, the reliability and Picos are the big pluses.

It easily connects with your wifi system using your phone and the MyLeviton app, where you can set up schedules for on and off times, including basing them on sundown or sunrise. For instance, I set mine to come on ten minutes after sunset and go off at 10:30pm, every day. Now, installation: Is this for a DIYer or for an electrician to install? If you know nothing about house wiring, don't plan on doing this yourself. Nothing wrong with how it's built, but you can run into interesting issues when you open a box with, say, three or four other switches in it. It may seem to have a confusing jumble of wires, the switch you're replacing may have no neutral (white) coming to it, and you'll need to figure out which wire goes to the source and which goes to the load. All that said, if you DO know what you're doing with house wiring, this is a snap to install (aside from the problems just mentioned). The switch is likely larger than the one you're replacing, and there may be scant room for it. The switch has wires coming out of it (i.e., no screw terminals or insert holes) that you attach to existing wiring with wire nuts, and you need to cram all that in the box. Note that this switch can be used in two-way or three-way configurations. Full disclosure, I have used it only in two-way on/off applications.

B0BVKZLT3B#23.review: Easy to set up with an on/off schedule... - First, Leviton is high quality, no question. This is not my first automatic Leviton switch, this was a second buy. This switch comes with a nice screwless wall plate, which you can use if you have a lone switch to replace. It easily connects with your wifi system using your phone and the MyLeviton app, where you can set up schedules for on and off times, including basing them on sundown or sunrise. For instance, I set mine to come on ten minutes after sunset and go off at 10:30pm, every day. Now, installation: Is this for a DIYer or for an electrician to install? If you know nothing about house wiring, don't plan on doing this yourself. Nothing wrong with how it's built, but you can run into interesting issues when you open a box with, say, three or four other switches in it. It may seem to have a confusing jumble of wires, the switch you're replacing may have no neutral (white) coming to it, and you'll need to figure out which wire goes to the source and which goes to the load. All that said, if you DO know what you're doing with house wiring, this is a snap to install (aside from the problems just mentioned). The switch is likely larger than the one you're replacing, and there may be scant room for it. The switch has wires coming out of it (i.e., no screw terminals or insert holes) that you attach to existing wiring with wire nuts, and you need to cram all that in the box. Note that this switch can be used in two-way or three-way configurations. Full disclosure, I have used it only in two-way on/off applications.

Love that I don't need hardwired Z-wave accessory switches anymore, and these make it so less crowded in a multi-gangbox! B0CZKYMVPR#28.review: Check your wiring first, but very convenient when it works - The thing you need to know before buying this switch remote and receiver is that the receiver requires four wires, which not every light switch box will have. It depends on how your lightswitch was installed. So, I recommend turning off the breaker and opening up the switch you want to move to check the wiring before ordering. Make sure there’s a cable with power coming in (live black wire and neutral white). This will power the receiver. If there are only two wires, then power is going to the fixture first, and the receiver won’t work. There also needs to be a cable with two wires going to the fixture. If there’s a third, red wire, you probably have a 3-way switch. Treewell does sell a receiver with two remotes for this situation (see my review of that below). I installed mine to move a switch for the light over our kitchen sink. The original switch was awkwardly placed behind where we keep our dish soap, etc. I put the new switch on the side of the cabinet above and to the right of the sink. It was great not to have to run wires or take up cabinet space with an electrical box. If you are moving a switch, you might want to go ahead and order a blank wall plate to match your box size and decor. At first, I thought it might feel wasteful to use a battery powered switch, but most ceiling fans have remotes now, so it’s not that unusual. I plan to install a garbage disposal, and I’m thinking about getting another one of these switches for that. Great product! ------------------------------------------------------------ Here's my review of the 3-way version (also 5 stars): Our new house has a Jack and Jill bathroom. The inspector said one of the light switches was too close to the bathtub. I was able to install this receiver where the old switch was and install the new remote switch on the other side of the doorway. The bathroom has pocket doors, so I wouldn’t have been able to move the switch to the new location without this product. I needed the version with 2 remotes because this is a 3-way switch. I couldn’t figure out the wiring to replace only 1 of the switches. So, I replaced them both. I capped off the extra wires going between the two switches (even though there’s no power going to those wires now). There was just enough room in the single-gang box to fit everything back inside. It’s nice that they include both bolts and screws/anchors to install the remote switch plates, allowing you to mount the plates to electrical boxes or the wall. I’m realizing now that I could also move the second switch inside the bathroom. I might do that later. This system is very flexible with lots of applications.

For many years, replacing a light switch was a no-brainer. Not in terms of being careless; one does not fool around with electricity (or plumbing). I mean in terms of going to the store and buying a Leviton light switch. Good quality and highly dependable. Well, I am sorry but I think something bad has happened in recent years at Leviton. In a nutshell, my experience is this: I have Leviton light switches that probably go back to when my house was new (circa 1980) and they go on and on, no problem. Never need replacing. However, with a handful of switches that did need replacing in recent years, I have needed to replace them more than once. Especially, in one case, a bathroom light switch. FOUR TIMES IN THE PAST TWO OR THREE YEARS. This is not a high-traffic area and there are no children playing with or abusing this switch. My wife and I are consciously taking it easy with this one, knowing that it keeps breaking. There is nothing in the way that it is installed that would account for it being fragile. Yet, here I was the other night, with my wife informing me that the bathroom light switch was broken again. This necessitated a trip to Home Depot which fortunately stays open until 10pm. And get this: A Home Depot employee approached me while I was looking for alternatives, offering me assistance. I asked him what in the heck is wrong with this type of Leviton light switch. "It keeps breaking?" he said. "Yes," I said. He did not say anything else in response but he did nod his head in agreement, like it's not the first time he has heard this. My theory is, some time in the past few years, Leviton decided to go with a lower-grade of plastic in order to save money. What else would account for this repeated failure? And it's not just a bad batch; I have gone to both Ace Hardware and Home Depot over a long enough period of time with the same bad results for replacing Leviton light switches in the bathroom and two other locations in my house. Unasked, the Home Depot guy recommended that I go with a rocker type of switch instead. "Better quality," was his advice. I hope so because it, too, is made by Leviton. For one thing is true: Leviton sure as heck has the local retail market sewn up. We may see alternatives here on Amazon but in places like Home Depot, Leviton is all that is available.

I mean in terms of going to the store and buying a Leviton light switch. Good quality and highly dependable. Well, I am sorry but I think something bad has happened in recent years at Leviton. In a nutshell, my experience is this: I have Leviton light switches that probably go back to when my house was new (circa 1980) and they go on and on, no problem. Never need replacing. However, with a handful of switches that did need replacing in recent years, I have needed to replace them more than once. Especially, in one case, a bathroom light switch. "It keeps breaking?" he said. "Yes," I said. He did not say anything else in response but he did nod his head in agreement, like it's not the first time he has heard this. My theory is, some time in the past few years, Leviton decided to go with a lower-grade of plastic in order to save money. What else would account for this repeated failure? And it's not just a bad batch; I have gone to both Ace Hardware and Home Depot over a long enough period of time with the same bad results for replacing Leviton light switches in the bathroom and two other locations in my house. Unasked, the Home Depot guy recommended that I go with a rocker type of switch instead. "Better quality," was his advice. I hope so because it, too, is made by Leviton. But these new Lutron switches are built (somehow) to accommodate LED, halogen and incandescent light, all of which I have in my home. I can only presume that the issue had something to do with the light bar of 8 bulbs but maybe it's the switch too. So caution. In replacing the worn-out, twist-prone Lutron switches with their new equally-adjustable counterparts, we've found that these switches are hard to fit into the electric boxes that were built 25-years ago. Fortunately Lutron has put sort of wings on the sides that you can break off to help you wedge the switch into the box. The problem really comes in when you have a 2-3-4 switch panel. We found it very hard to get these switches to fit in in those 2-3-4 switch panels and even harder to keep from breaking the lovely cover for the boxes. Perhaps that is why Lutron's 4-swich unit has no screws on it since aligning screws with the 4-panel is guaranteed breakage. We decided instead, since we couldn't figure out from the Amazon posting how the screwless unit was attached, that we would just glue the old cover back together and ignore the crack it left. You know these Lutron switches are about to go when (consistently) they begin to shift sideways and the contact points become erratic. Don't wait to replace; it will not stay the same or get better. It's not something you did; it's a flaw of the switch. ... B07HM6L48C#23.review: New to Lutron (but have 24 years of automated light switches) - Learned Some Important Things.. - Just recently switch to Lutron product line, and my fan switch install went flawless. I installed this switch on my outdoor lights and learned a lot along the way. Hopefully this will help someone else. - When I installed the switch, I have neutral wires in my gangboxes (house built in 2000), and was shocked that this switch didn't have a neutral connection. You don't need it for this switch, which is great for those that don't have the wire, but it was a first for me as my Zwave switches always needed it - Switch was installed correctly, but had no lights on the switch itself, and while I noticed my outdoor porch lights were showing a dimly lit bulb, hitting the on or off on the switch did nothing. I was convinced initially it was wiring, but lo and behold, the true issue was the bulbs that I installed. I had purchased some cheap no-name brand LED bulbs and they were not dimmable (I think). Upon changing the bulb, the switch showed operational lights, and everything worked fine. In my two fixtures, I initially only changed one, and that was all it took to get it working. I confirmed the same issue when I installed another switch for my 3 deck post lights. Changing a bulb to a dimmable bulb (while I wait for matching replacements) was all I needed to do to get it to work! - Pico remotes are amazing, and can be used for many different things. Love that I don't need hardwired Z-wave accessory switches anymore, and these make it so less crowded in a multi-gangbox! Highly recommend those looking to make the switch from Zwave, WiFi and other lower quality switches. I will say my Zwave installation was flawless in operation, but ultimately got sick of the low quality and frequent failures. Anyone considering a "WiFi" switch should not do so, but I'm not going to gain much in functionality over my Zwave switches, the reliability and Picos are the big pluses.

B085D8M2MR#16.review: Some installation problems and a 20-year lifespan - I've used all different kinds of these gorgeous and highly adjustable Lutron switches (primarily exactly like these) for 25 years. And that's just about how long they last, which is a disappointment to me because the old-fashioned narrow flip on/off switches last as long as the building stands. But these new Lutron switches are built (somehow) to accommodate LED, halogen and incandescent light, all of which I have in my home. I do have a light bar that we replaced with LED bulbs and these new LED switches allowed a mind-numbing flicker of light that is so bad that I'm replacing the energy-sucking, hot incandescent bulbs there. I can only presume that the issue had something to do with the light bar of 8 bulbs but maybe it's the switch too. So caution. In replacing the worn-out, twist-prone Lutron switches with their new equally-adjustable counterparts, we've found that these switches are hard to fit into the electric boxes that were built 25-years ago. Fortunately Lutron has put sort of wings on the sides that you can break off to help you wedge the switch into the box. The problem really comes in when you have a 2-3-4 switch panel. We found it very hard to get these switches to fit in in those 2-3-4 switch panels and even harder to keep from breaking the lovely cover for the boxes. Perhaps that is why Lutron's 4-swich unit has no screws on it since aligning screws with the 4-panel is guaranteed breakage. We decided instead, since we couldn't figure out from the Amazon posting how the screwless unit was attached, that we would just glue the old cover back together and ignore the crack it left. You know these Lutron switches are about to go when (consistently) they begin to shift sideways and the contact points become erratic. Don't wait to replace; it will not stay the same or get better. It's not something you did; it's a flaw of the switch. ... But they sure make the house feel nice and for a person who is all about light, it's odd and intensity, in the end, Lutron is a dream come true..

B095X5HTLS#37.review: YMMV: Did not work with only my LED fixture and a traditional 3 way switch in the circuit - I was a little leery that the online description as of 04/06/24 said this switch uses just one traveler wire. 3 way circuits always have two travelers. But I wanted to check it out their innovation as I have Amazon plugs and Echos in my house. I have also installed multiple single pole and 3 way smart switches from other brands. I know how to wire two travelers, I've got neutral wires, and my existing setup had two working standard 3 way switches that functioned just fine. BTW, the included instructions showed a different wiring setup than the one in the product description. Unfortunately, neither worked for my setup. 5 stars for innovation reduced to 1 star for execution. The positive: once it was hooked up, Alexa did automatically sense the switch, connect to WiFi, and add it to My Devices. The negatives: I was never able to get the switch to function as designed with my LED fixture, the Amazon switch, and a standard switch in the circuit. I am assuming this may have something to do with the low power draw or the dimmer function (not likely, I know). In the best wiring configuration - I tried them all - I could turn the fixture on and off from the Alexa app - but once I used the standard switch it turned off and would only flicker on briefly when I flipped the standard switch. Also, when the fixture was lit it buzzed (search for the other brands that use the technology that eliminates this). No shorts, not incorrect wiring. I disconnected all the wiring, started from scratch, and used an NCV and a meter to confirm the continuity on each wire. Same results. I swapped the smart switch with the standard switch just in case I incorrectly identified the "load" side. Same results. I put the old standard 3 way switch back and everything worked with no buzz. Insanity is trying the same thing over and over with the same results. So I am returning this switch and suggest that if you are using a single low power LED fixture and a standard switch you try a smart switch that accommodates two travelers in its wiring, doesn't need to be on the "load" side, and doesn't cause buzzing.
aspects: 34583#connectivity: did not work with LED fixture and traditional 3 way switch

B08RRM8VH5#40.review: A reasonable replacement for the seemingly deprecated DG6HD - TLDR: This is working well with Matter and Home Assistant over wifi; if I have any issues with reliability I will update. Note: I have many Zigbee "gen 1" Leviton dimmers DG6HD. They are still (mostly) my favorite excepting two things, 1 they seem to be at least softly discontinued, not advertised anymore and hard to find in stock, 2: the D26HD supports double tap to max brightness, which the Zigbee DG6HD does not have. Because of these 2 reasons, I reluctantly tried the D26HD and find it an acceptable alternative; however, I'd still prefer a Thread or Zigbee-based version as D26HD requires a My Leviton account, access to your wifi, access to your precision location on your mobile, access to your wi-fi password, and Internet access, and is harder to set up than Zigbee switches for those who know what is Zigbee and have a Zigbee hub. If you want Matter you have to use My Leviton to set it up first, opt into Matter early access, and upgrade your firmware. This was "easy enough". Not as easy as Zigbee you click one button in Home Assistant and done though. The Zigbee versions also allow access to fade in/out timers, but Matter mode does not, at least in HA as of writing this review; however, you can configure it via My Leviton app. I have not yet tested if the device works when restricted from the Internet in Matter mode. I use this with the DD00R companion for multi-location dimming. I did not want to use the "anywhere" battery-operated switches so utilized existing multi-pole wiring. Wiring is standard. Compared to DG6HD's screw terminals the D26HD uses pigtails -- some find this as a pro, some as con. B07HM6L48C#23.review: New to Lutron (but have 24 years of automated light switches) - Learned Some Important Things.. - Just recently switch to Lutron product line, and my fan switch install went flawless. I was convinced initially it was wiring, but lo and behold, the true issue was the bulbs that I installed. I had purchased some cheap no-name brand LED bulbs and they were not dimmable (I think). B08RRM8VH5#40.review: A reasonable replacement for the seemingly deprecated DG6HD - TLDR: This is working well with Matter and Home Assistant over wifi; if I have any issues with reliability I will update. Note: I have many Zigbee "gen 1" Leviton dimmers DG6HD. They are still (mostly) my favorite excepting two things, 1 they seem to be at least softly discontinued, not advertised anymore and hard to find in stock, 2: the D26HD supports double tap to max brightness, which the Zigbee DG6HD does not have. Because of these 2 reasons, I reluctantly tried the D26HD and find it an acceptable alternative; however, I'd still prefer a Thread or Zigbee-based version as D26HD requires a My Leviton account, access to your wifi, access to your precision location on your mobile, access to your wi-fi password, and Internet access, and is harder to set up than Zigbee switches for those who know what is Zigbee and have a Zigbee hub. If you want Matter you have to use My Leviton to set it up first, opt into Matter early access, and upgrade your firmware. This was "easy enough". Not as easy as Zigbee you click one button in Home Assistant and done though. The Zigbee versions also allow access to fade in/out timers, but Matter mode does not, at least in HA as of writing this review; however, you can configure it via My Leviton app. I have not yet tested if the device works when restricted from the Internet in Matter mode. I use this with the DD00R companion for multi-location dimming. I did not want to use the "anywhere" battery-operated switches so utilized existing multi-pole wiring. Wiring is standard. Compared to DG6HD's screw terminals the D26HD uses pigtails -- some find this as a pro, some as con. The DD00R is compatible with the double tap to max on / off, which surprised me since it was made for gen 1 devices that don't support it; HOWEVER, if you double tap the DD00R quickly it recognizes as a single tap while on the D26HD it works perfectly. Using remote control via My Leviton and via Matter through Home Assistant appears instant. I opted to use My Leviton as little as possible so I use Google Assistant integration via Home Assistant instead of My Leviton. In Home Assistant Matter only the on/off and dim level is supported, which for me supports all everyday use case. In My Leviton you can change bulb type, min and max dim power levels, and fade on and fade off time settings in 0.5 second increments and upgrade firmware, which is a "one time" expected use for me. In general, I am anti-wifi for smart devices due to the lower reliability I've typically witnessed and inappropriate for battery-powered devices, but as a wired device it is OK enough, although if Leviton drops cloud support you lose the advanced configuration functionality. I still prefer the privacy-centric features and cloud-free Zigbee DG6HD, but again they seem to be on the way out. A great improvement will be when Matter comes out-of-the-box so you can enroll it without Internet or My Leviton, and if the advanced features can be supported (if possible) via Matter.

But these new Lutron switches are built (somehow) to accommodate LED, halogen and incandescent light, all of which I have in my home. I do have a light bar that we replaced with LED bulbs and these new LED switches allowed a mind-numbing flicker of light that is so bad that I'm replacing the energy-sucking, hot incandescent bulbs there. I can only presume that the issue had something to do with the light bar of 8 bulbs but maybe it's the switch too. So caution. In replacing the worn-out, twist-prone Lutron switches with their new equally-adjustable counterparts, we've found that these switches are hard to fit into the electric boxes that were built 25-years ago. Fortunately Lutron has put sort of wings on the sides that you can break off to help you wedge the switch into the box. The problem really comes in when you have a 2-3-4 switch panel. We found it very hard to get these switches to fit in in those 2-3-4 switch panels and even harder to keep from breaking the lovely cover for the boxes. Perhaps that is why Lutron's 4-swich unit has no screws on it since aligning screws with the 4-panel is guaranteed breakage. We decided instead, since we couldn't figure out from the Amazon posting how the screwless unit was attached, that we would just glue the old cover back together and ignore the crack it left. You know these Lutron switches are about to go when (consistently) they begin to shift sideways and the contact points become erratic. Don't wait to replace; it will not stay the same or get better. It's not something you did; it's a flaw of the switch. ... B08RRM8VH5#40.review: A reasonable replacement for the seemingly deprecated DG6HD - TLDR: This is working well with Matter and Home Assistant over wifi; if I have any issues with reliability I will update. Note: I have many Zigbee "gen 1" Leviton dimmers DG6HD. They are still (mostly) my favorite excepting two things, 1 they seem to be at least softly discontinued, not advertised anymore and hard to find in stock, 2: the D26HD supports double tap to max brightness, which the Zigbee DG6HD does not have. Because of these 2 reasons, I reluctantly tried the D26HD and find it an acceptable alternative; however, I'd still prefer a Thread or Zigbee-based version as D26HD requires a My Leviton account, access to your wifi, access to your precision location on your mobile, access to your wi-fi password, and Internet access, and is harder to set up than Zigbee switches for those who know what is Zigbee and have a Zigbee hub. If you want Matter you have to use My Leviton to set it up first, opt into Matter early access, and upgrade your firmware. This was "easy enough". Not as easy as Zigbee you click one button in Home Assistant and done though. The Zigbee versions also allow access to fade in/out timers, but Matter mode does not, at least in HA as of writing this review; however, you can configure it via My Leviton app. I have not yet tested if the device works when restricted from the Internet in Matter mode. I use this with the DD00R companion for multi-location dimming. I did not want to use the "anywhere" battery-operated switches so utilized existing multi-pole wiring. Wiring is standard. Compared to DG6HD's screw terminals the D26HD uses pigtails -- some find this as a pro, some as con. The DD00R is compatible with the double tap to max on / off, which surprised me since it was made for gen 1 devices that don't support it; HOWEVER, if you double tap the DD00R quickly it recognizes as a single tap while on the D26HD it works perfectly. Using remote control via My Leviton and via Matter through Home Assistant appears instant. I opted to use My Leviton as little as possible so I use Google Assistant integration via Home Assistant instead of My Leviton. In Home Assistant Matter only the on/off and dim level is supported, which for me supports all everyday use case. In My Leviton you can change bulb type, min and max dim power levels, and fade on and fade off time settings in 0.5 second increments and upgrade firmware, which is a "one time" expected use for me. In general, I am anti-wifi for smart devices due to the lower reliability I've typically witnessed and inappropriate for battery-powered devices, but as a wired device it is OK enough, although if Leviton drops cloud support you lose the advanced configuration functionality. I still prefer the privacy-centric features and cloud-free Zigbee DG6HD, but again they seem to be on the way out. A great improvement will be when Matter comes out-of-the-box so you can enroll it without Internet or My Leviton, and if the advanced features can be supported (if possible) via Matter.
aspects: 31241#configuration: can configure fade timers via My Leviton app

B08RRM8VH5#10.review: Excellent Quality and Features - Reviewing "Dimmer": Replacing old WiFi dimmer in Master Bedroom. My critical feature was that it would dim low. I bought two new ones previous to this; one dimmed to maybe 30%, the next to maybe 20%, this one I would say went to 10%. I decided that was the best I was going to get and was acceptable. Besides that aspect, this is a great dimmer - definitely the best of all I tried. I like that it is a push top to turn on, bottom to turn off switch (dimmer adjustment is on the right). I really like that the locator light when the switch is turned off is very dim (some are just too bright for a bedroom). The instructions and software are top par, very high quality, and the software allows for a lot of adjustment and customization. The only issue I had was with Matter. I did the software update and got it hooked up, but it kept disconnecting from Alexa. I didn't pursue a fix to this and instead opted to hook it up to Alexa through the app - which worked fine and no disconnecting issues since. If you're looking for something basic and/or if being able to dim very low is not important to you, you'll find other products on Amazon that will do the job decently for less money. If you are hard set on Matter, read a different review, but if not and you want top of the line and are willing to pay for it, this is a definite buy.

B095X5HTLS#37.review: YMMV: Did not work with only my LED fixture and a traditional 3 way switch in the circuit - I was a little leery that the online description as of 04/06/24 said this switch uses just one traveler wire. 3 way circuits always have two travelers. But I wanted to check it out their innovation as I have Amazon plugs and Echos in my house. I have also installed multiple single pole and 3 way smart switches from other brands. I know how to wire two travelers, I've got neutral wires, and my existing setup had two working standard 3 way switches that functioned just fine. BTW, the included instructions showed a different wiring setup than the one in the product description. Unfortunately, neither worked for my setup. 5 stars for innovation reduced to 1 star for execution. The positive: once it was hooked up, Alexa did automatically sense the switch, connect to WiFi, and add it to My Devices. The negatives: I was never able to get the switch to function as designed with my LED fixture, the Amazon switch, and a standard switch in the circuit. I am assuming this may have something to do with the low power draw or the dimmer function (not likely, I know). In the best wiring configuration - I tried them all - I could turn the fixture on and off from the Alexa app - but once I used the standard switch it turned off and would only flicker on briefly when I flipped the standard switch. Also, when the fixture was lit it buzzed (search for the other brands that use the technology that eliminates this). No shorts, not incorrect wiring. I disconnected all the wiring, started from scratch, and used an NCV and a meter to confirm the continuity on each wire. Same results. I swapped the smart switch with the standard switch just in case I incorrectly identified the "load" side. Same results. I put the old standard 3 way switch back and everything worked with no buzz. Insanity is trying the same thing over and over with the same results. So I am returning this switch and suggest that if you are using a single low power LED fixture and a standard switch you try a smart switch that accommodates two travelers in its wiring, doesn't need to be on the "load" side, and doesn't cause buzzing.

It may seem to have a confusing jumble of wires, the switch you're replacing may have no neutral (white) coming to it, and you'll need to figure out which wire goes to the source and which goes to the load. All that said, if you DO know what you're doing with house wiring, this is a snap to install (aside from the problems just mentioned). The switch is likely larger than the one you're replacing, and there may be scant room for it. The switch has wires coming out of it (i.e., no screw terminals or insert holes) that you attach to existing wiring with wire nuts, and you need to cram all that in the box. Note that this switch can be used in two-way or three-way configurations. Full disclosure, I have used it only in two-way on/off applications.

Note: I have many Zigbee "gen 1" Leviton dimmers DG6HD. They are still (mostly) my favorite excepting two things, 1 they seem to be at least softly discontinued, not advertised anymore and hard to find in stock, 2: the D26HD supports double tap to max brightness, which the Zigbee DG6HD does not have. Because of these 2 reasons, I reluctantly tried the D26HD and find it an acceptable alternative; however, I'd still prefer a Thread or Zigbee-based version as D26HD requires a My Leviton account, access to your wifi, access to your precision location on your mobile, access to your wi-fi password, and Internet access, and is harder to set up than Zigbee switches for those who know what is Zigbee and have a Zigbee hub. If you want Matter you have to use My Leviton to set it up first, opt into Matter early access, and upgrade your firmware. This was "easy enough". Not as easy as Zigbee you click one button in Home Assistant and done though. The Zigbee versions also allow access to fade in/out timers, but Matter mode does not, at least in HA as of writing this review; however, you can configure it via My Leviton app. I have not yet tested if the device works when restricted from the Internet in Matter mode. I use this with the DD00R companion for multi-location dimming. I did not want to use the "anywhere" battery-operated switches so utilized existing multi-pole wiring. Wiring is standard. Compared to DG6HD's screw terminals the D26HD uses pigtails -- some find this as a pro, some as con. The DD00R is compatible with the double tap to max on / off, which surprised me since it was made for gen 1 devices that don't support it; HOWEVER, if you double tap the DD00R quickly it recognizes as a single tap while on the D26HD it works perfectly. Using remote control via My Leviton and via Matter through Home Assistant appears instant. I opted to use My Leviton as little as possible so I use Google Assistant integration via Home Assistant instead of My Leviton. In Home Assistant Matter only the on/off and dim level is supported, which for me supports all everyday use case. In My Leviton you can change bulb type, min and max dim power levels, and fade on and fade off time settings in 0.5 second increments and upgrade firmware, which is a "one time" expected use for me. In general, I am anti-wifi for smart devices due to the lower reliability I've typically witnessed and inappropriate for battery-powered devices, but as a wired device it is OK enough, although if Leviton drops cloud support you lose the advanced configuration functionality. I still prefer the privacy-centric features and cloud-free Zigbee DG6HD, but again they seem to be on the way out. A great improvement will be when Matter comes out-of-the-box so you can enroll it without Internet or My Leviton, and if the advanced features can be supported (if possible) via Matter.
